caption:
Prateep Basu spent years building satellites for ISRO. Then he started a company to point them at crop fields and flood zones instead.

In 2017, Basu co-founded SatSure in Bengaluru, using satellite data to help banks, insurers, and governments make decisions about agriculture, infrastructure, and disaster response. One of its earliest wins was a crop-insurance contract with the Andhra Pradesh government, applied for from Switzerland just before the deadline.

SatSure just raised Rs 60 crore from a government-backed space fund as part of an ongoing round, valuing the company at roughly Rs 870 crore - with private banks also lining up to invest in what satellite data can tell them about risk on the ground.

He didn't leave space behind. He just pointed it at problems closer to home.

Sources: Business Standard, The Ken
